questions.question: Which is the fully qualified name of Scanner?
questions.explanation: Scanner is the simple class name and java.util is its package.
optionFeedback: A filename is not a fully qualified type name.
Scanner is not declared in java.lang.
Correct: package plus simple name.
Package names do not include the source-file extension.

questions.question: What does an import allow?
options: Using a type's simple name in that source file
Running the class without a classpath
questions.explanation: Imports participate in source name resolution only.
optionFeedback: Correct: the type can be referenced without repeating its package.
Dependencies must already be available.
Access modifiers are unaffected.
Runtime class loading still needs a correct classpath.

questions.question: Which pair of packages supplies FileReader and Scanner?
questions.explanation: FileReader is java.io.FileReader; Scanner is java.util.Scanner.
optionFeedback: Correct: imports must cover both packages.
FileReader is not java.lang and Scanner is not java.io.
FileReader is not in either of these packages.
Scanner is not in java.io.

questions.question: What can be called after import static java.lang.Math.sqrt;?
questions.explanation: A static import makes the member's short name available.
optionFeedback: Scanner is unrelated and nextLine needs an instance.
Correct: sqrt is the imported static method.
Math is not constructed to call this static member.
sqrt belongs to Math, not directly to the package.

questions.question: After new Book[50] and two new Book(...) assignments, how many Book objects exist?
questions.explanation: The array contains references; only the two constructor calls create Books.
optionFeedback: Array allocation does not construct every element.
The array is not a Book, and unfilled cells remain null.
Correct: two Books plus a separate array object.
There is one array but two Book instances.

questions.question: A file imports BufferedReader only. Can it use FileReader by simple name?
options: No, it needs another import or the fully qualified name
questions.explanation: A single-type import makes one name available, not all its package peers.
optionFeedback: Common package membership does not extend the import.
Source names must resolve before execution.
OS does not change Java imports.
Correct: import java.io.FileReader or qualify it.

questions.question: Does `import java.util.*;` import TimeUnit from java.util.concurrent?
questions.explanation: The wildcard covers public types directly in java.util, not types in a subpackage.
optionFeedback: Java imports do not recurse into subpackages.
Correct: java.util.concurrent needs its own import.
Operating system does not change import semantics.
Public access is necessary but does not make a subpackage recursive.

questions.question: Two packages provide a class named Date. How can one source file use both?
options: Use a fully qualified name for at least one
questions.explanation: A fully qualified reference removes ambiguity by naming the package explicitly.
optionFeedback: Two single-type imports with the same simple name conflict.
Correct: qualification identifies the intended Date.
Imports cannot appear inside a method.
Runtime renaming is not how Java resolves the source names.

questions.question: Two wildcard imports, java.util.* and java.sql.*, are present. When does the Date ambiguity matter?
options: Whenever Date is used as an unresolved simple name
Both imports are immediately illegal even without using Date
questions.explanation: On-demand imports can coexist; using the ambiguous simple type name requires disambiguation.
optionFeedback: Correct: fully qualify the intended Date.
That confuses wildcard imports with conflicting single-type imports.
Platform does not decide type-name lookup.
Import order does not choose an owner here.

questions.question: What detects EOF in the BufferedReader example?
questions.explanation: No remaining line is represented by null, not an empty record.
optionFeedback: count begins at zero for all files.
Correct: stop before parsing null.
An empty line can occur before EOF.
Constructors do not return this search sentinel.

questions.question: Why display only while i < count after two Book records?
options: To avoid accessor calls through null cells
questions.explanation: Unfilled cells beyond the populated count remain null.
optionFeedback: Try-with-resources closes the file.
Iteration does not rename types.
Correct: stop before the unfilled portion.
Displaying is not sorting.

questions.question: Why check count < books.length before reading another record in an && condition?
options: Short-circuiting prevents another read/store once full
questions.explanation: A false capacity guard skips the read expression and prevents writing beyond the last cell.
optionFeedback: Imports and loop guards solve different problems.
Arrays retain fixed length.
A shorter input creates fewer Books.
Correct: guard capacity before reading and storing.
